title: What can a sandboxed command reach?
intro: The sandbox is on in auto-allow mode, with registry.npmjs.org as the only allowed domain. Type a command Claude runs.

show.title: Allowed
show.detail: The domain is on network.allowedDomains, so the request goes through the sandbox's proxy.

show.title: Network blocked
show.detail: The domain isn't on network.allowedDomains, so the sandbox refuses the connection.

trace.text: Domain not allowed: the connection fails.

show.title: Write blocked
show.detail: Commands can write only inside the project, a temporary folder and added directories. The system refuses a write elsewhere, for example with Operation not permitted on macOS.

trace.text: Write outside the allowed folders: Operation not permitted.

show.title: Runs without a prompt
show.detail: The command stays inside the project folder, so in auto-allow mode it runs straight away. The sandbox would stop it if it tried to step outside.

trace.text: Runs inside the limits: no prompt needed.

fallback.title: Type a command first
fallback.detail: This demo scripts a few cases: downloads from allowed and other domains, writes outside the project, and commands that stay inside it.

quiz.question: Which of these runs outside the sandbox?
options: A process started by a shell command
quiz.explanation: The sandbox wraps shell commands and their child processes. Built-in file tools, hooks and local MCP servers run outside it, so permission rules still matter.
